hunks.baseline: The world was submerged in a darkness so deep that it was impossible to tell how much time had passed.
hunks.sol: The world lay submerged in darkness so deep that it was impossible to tell how much time had passed.

hunks.baseline: The sky was filled with black clouds, and the rain that had seemed like a passing shower refused to stop.
hunks.sol: Black clouds filled the sky, and the rain that had seemed like a passing shower showed no sign of stopping.

hunks.baseline: Within the grounds of the Sichuan Tang Clan, near a puddle of spilled blood, corpses had piled up into a small hill.
hunks.sol: Within the grounds of the Sichuan Tang Clan, beside an overflowing pool of blood, corpses had piled up into a small hill.

hunks.baseline: At the gates of the Sichuan Tang Clan, a black-clad man was sitting astride the corpse of an unknown Tang Clan martial artist. A subordinate who had just arrived from the Inner Hall answered his question.
hunks.sol: At the gates of the Sichuan Tang Clan, a black-clad man sat astride the corpse of an unknown Tang Clan martial artist. A subordinate who had just arrived from the Inner Hall answered him.

hunks.baseline: “The situation still hasn’t ended. I hear about a hundred of them are left.”
hunks.sol: “It still isn’t over. I hear about a hundred of them remain.”

hunks.baseline: “Only half of them are martial artists. The rest are craftsmen who haven’t learned martial arts, women, or children.”
hunks.sol: “Only half are martial artists. The rest are craftsmen who never learned martial arts, women, or children.”

hunks.baseline: “Then they should just wipe them out without a second thought. What kind of pointless nonsense are they doing?”
hunks.sol: “Then they should wipe them out and be done with it. What the hell are they wasting time for?”

hunks.baseline: The black-clad man’s dissatisfaction was only natural. It was unpleasant enough to be stuck guarding the entrance while others made accomplishments. The fact that this tedious gatekeeping still had not ended irritated him even more.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man’s irritation was only natural. Being stuck guarding the entrance while the others earned all the glory was bad enough, but this tedious gate duty still wasn’t over.

hunks.baseline: Seeing his superior frown, the subordinate hurriedly continued.
hunks.sol: At his superior’s frown, the subordinate hurriedly continued.

hunks.baseline: “The surviving Tang Clan martial artists are elites, for one thing. But it seems the Tang Clan activated a mechanism array, which has delayed things.”
hunks.sol: “The surviving Tang Clan martial artists are elites, for one thing. But the real problem is that they activated a mechanism array, and it’s holding everyone up.”

hunks.baseline: “A mechanism array? If it’s a poison array, it shouldn’t be difficult to break through.”
hunks.sol: “A mechanism array? A poison array shouldn’t be difficult to break through.”

hunks.baseline: “It isn’t poison. It’s explosives. They had hidden Heaven-Shaking Thunder.”
hunks.sol: “It isn’t poison. It’s explosives. They had Heaven-Shaking Thunder hidden away.”

hunks.baseline: “……You don’t mean the Heaven-Shaking Thunder of the Pyeokryeomun,[^1] do you?”
hunks.sol: “……You don’t mean the Heaven-Shaking Thunder from the Pyeokryeomun, do you?”

hunks.baseline: [^1]: The Pyeokryeomun was a martial sect that had been destroyed long ago.

hunks.baseline: “It seems so. Because some of them charged in carrying Heaven-Shaking Thunder and died in the explosions, quite a few of our brothers suffered serious losses.”
hunks.sol: “It seems so. Some of them charged in carrying Heaven-Shaking Thunder and blew themselves up. Quite a few of our brothers were caught in the blasts.”

hunks.baseline: The black-clad man’s mouth fell open. He had wondered what was happening when the ominous booms began echoing around them. He had never expected the Tang Clan to possess Heaven-Shaking Thunder from the Pyeokryeomun, a sect that had been destroyed long ago.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man’s mouth fell open. He had wondered what was happening when those ominous booms began echoing through the grounds, but he had never expected the Tang Clan to possess Heaven-Shaking Thunder from the long-destroyed Pyeokryeomun.

hunks.baseline: He could now understand, to some extent, why the battle had been delayed.
hunks.sol: Now he could understand why the battle had dragged on.

hunks.baseline: “Wait. Then what has the Demon Lord been doing? He should have been able to slaughter them all by himself.”
hunks.sol: “Wait. Then what has the Demon Lord been doing? He should have been more than capable of slaughtering them all himself.”

hunks.baseline: The black-clad man’s question was founded on his unwavering faith in the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man’s question reflected his unwavering faith in the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

hunks.baseline: That was only natural. The Western Heaven Demon Lord was one of the few servants permitted to pay respects to the exalted Lord of Heaven, and he possessed terrifying martial might.
hunks.sol: And for good reason. The Western Heaven Demon Lord was one of the few servants permitted an audience with the exalted Lord of Heaven, and he possessed terrifying martial might.

hunks.baseline: The black-clad man did not know how powerful the Heaven-Shaking Thunder he had only heard about was. But even if the grandfather of Heaven-Shaking Thunder itself appeared, it would not be able to harm the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man had only ever heard of Heaven-Shaking Thunder and had no idea how powerful it truly was. But even the grandfather of Heaven-Shaking Thunder itself could never harm the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

hunks.baseline: “I heard he went to the Tang Clan’s underground prison an hour ago.”
hunks.sol: “I heard he went to the Tang Clan’s underground prison a shichen ago.”

hunks.baseline: The subordinate’s answer made the black-clad man nod.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man nodded.

hunks.baseline: If the Demon Lord had moved personally, there had to be a reason. He would resolve the matter without the slightest mistake. The black-clad man felt not even a trace of worry or doubt.
hunks.sol: If the Demon Lord had gone there personally, he must have had a reason, and he would resolve the matter without the slightest mistake. The black-clad man felt not a trace of worry or doubt.

hunks.baseline: Nor was that thought unique to him. Everyone felt the same way.
hunks.sol: Nor was he alone. Everyone felt the same way.

hunks.baseline: First Captain was the post that First Fiend, the eldest of the Qilian Three Fiends, had assumed upon entering the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s service.
hunks.sol: First Captain was the position First Fiend, the eldest of the Qilian Three Fiends, had assumed upon entering the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s service.

hunks.baseline: After hesitating briefly, the subordinate answered.
hunks.sol: After a brief hesitation, the subordinate answered.

hunks.baseline: “He’s engaged in a life-and-death duel with the Sword Saint’s successor in the Inner Hall. No one has been able to approach him since one of our brothers who went to deliver news about the Heaven-Shaking Thunder lost his head.”
hunks.sol: “He’s fighting a life-and-death duel with the Sword Saint’s successor in the Inner Hall. No one has dared approach since he took the head of the brother who went to inform him about the Heaven-Shaking Thunder.”

hunks.baseline: If his feelings toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord were reverence and trust, what he felt toward First Fiend was fear. He had no desire to complain carelessly and meet a horrible end.
hunks.sol: What he felt toward the Western Heaven Demon Lord was reverence and trust. What he felt toward First Fiend was fear. He had no desire to voice a careless complaint and meet a gruesome end.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. The deputy captain asked about the brothers who went to Qingcheng and Emei.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. The deputy captain asked whether we’d heard from the brothers sent to Qingcheng and Emei.”

hunks.baseline: The black-clad man handed him a small tube. After checking its contents, the subordinate raised his head with a bewildered expression.
hunks.sol: The black-clad man handed him a small tube. The subordinate checked its contents, then looked up in confusion.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. We still haven’t received anything from Qingcheng.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. We still haven’t heard anything from Qingcheng.”

hunks.baseline: “I believe the time for it to arrive has already passed.”
hunks.sol: “Their message should have arrived by now.”

hunks.baseline: The three brothers of the Qilian Three Fiends resembled one another in more than their ugly appearances.
hunks.sol: The three Qilian brothers resembled one another in more than their ugly faces.

hunks.baseline: They were all cruel and eccentric, fiends who went wild at the sight of blood.
hunks.sol: All three were cruel and eccentric fiends who lost their minds at the sight of blood.

hunks.baseline: The Third Fiend, who had been assigned to Emei Sect, was somewhat better than the others. At least he had sent a messenger eagle at the appointed time.
hunks.sol: Third Fiend, who had been assigned to Emei Sect, was somewhat better than the others. At least he had sent a messenger eagle at the appointed time.

hunks.baseline: The problem was that the situation described in the letter from Emei was not progressing smoothly.
hunks.sol: The problem was that, according to his letter, the situation at Emei was not proceeding smoothly.

hunks.baseline: The letter said that Beggars’ Sect disciples carrying bamboo staffs and dog clubs had suddenly appeared.
hunks.sol: The letter reported that Beggars’ Sect disciples wielding bamboo staffs and dog-beating clubs had appeared out of nowhere.

hunks.baseline: Their individual martial arts could not compare to those of Dark Heaven’s martial artists, but the meaning behind their appearance was significant.
hunks.sol: Individually, their martial arts were no match for Dark Heaven’s martial artists, but their appearance held greater significance.

hunks.baseline: The attack had been calculated down to the last detail. A battle that should have ended quickly was dragging on. Even so, the black-clad man had no doubt that their side would win despite this unexpected variable.
hunks.sol: The attack had been meticulously planned. The battle should have ended swiftly and decisively, yet it was dragging on.
Even with this unexpected complication, however, the black-clad man had no doubt that his side would prevail.

hunks.baseline: Just as he was casting off the unease that had briefly touched him, he suddenly raised his head.
hunks.sol: He had just shaken off the unease that had briefly troubled him when he suddenly looked up.

hunks.baseline: At the black-clad man’s questioning voice, not only the subordinate who had brought news from the Inner Hall but also the thirty-odd martial artists scattered at regular intervals to guard the walls gathered around their superior.
hunks.sol: At the black-clad man’s questioning voice, both the subordinate from the Inner Hall and the thirty-odd martial artists stationed at regular intervals along the walls gathered around him.

hunks.baseline: And soon, they saw it.
hunks.sol: Then they saw it.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the collapsed wall, a streak of wind cutting through the sheets of rain.
hunks.sol: Beyond the collapsed wall, a streak of wind tore through the driving rain.

hunks.baseline: It moved fast enough to be called a ray of light. Then it burst into a dazzling flash.
hunks.sol: It moved swiftly enough to be called a ray of light. Then it erupted in a dazzling flash.

hunks.baseline: The thirty-odd martial artists blinked. When they reflexively touched their faces, sticky blood came away on their fingers.
hunks.sol: The thirty-odd martial artists blinked. When they reflexively touched their faces, their fingers came away sticky with blood.

hunks.baseline: In the slowed-down world, they saw their superior’s body collapse like a rotten old tree.
hunks.sol: In a world that seemed to have slowed to a crawl, they watched their superior collapse like a rotten old tree.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if something had struck them across the backs of their heads.
hunks.sol: They felt as though they had been clubbed across the backs of their heads.

hunks.baseline: Their superior was a Peak master capable of making a name for himself anywhere under heaven. And yet a man with such skill had met his death from a blow they could not even see.
hunks.sol: Their superior was a Peak master capable of making a name for himself anywhere under heaven. Yet a man of such skill had been killed by a strike none of them had even seen.

hunks.baseline: Before anyone present could recover from that tremendous shock, a figure sprang up onto the wall.
hunks.sol: Before anyone could recover from the shock, a figure soared above the wall.

hunks.baseline: In the darkness, rays of light filled with death plunged down like lightning.
hunks.sol: In the darkness, death-laden rays of light plunged down like bolts of lightning.

hunks.baseline: No—he had already been insane for more than fifty years. He was merely becoming even more of a lunatic.
hunks.sol: No—he had already been insane for more than fifty years. Now he was becoming an even greater lunatic.

hunks.baseline: “Why! Why! How could this be!”
hunks.sol: “Why? Why? How!”

hunks.baseline: The sturdy pavilion where the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan had once lived had long since become a ruin.
hunks.sol: The sturdy pavilion where the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan had once resided had long since been reduced to ruins.

hunks.baseline: A figure was darting back and forth through it.
hunks.sol: A lone figure darted back and forth through the wreckage.

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung hopped and skipped around, dodging the Force with strange noises. First Fiend’s eyes rolled white.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung hopped and skipped around, dodging the Force while making strange noises. First Fiend’s eyes rolled white.

hunks.baseline: “You fucking bas—!”
hunks.sol: “You little son of a—!”

hunks.baseline: His opponent was a blood-brat who was not yet thirty. No matter how unprecedented a monster he was—a man who had received the Sword Saint’s teachings and reached the Supreme Peak realm in his twenties—the gap that came from age could not simply be ignored.
hunks.sol: His opponent was a mere pup not yet thirty. He might have been an unprecedented monster who had received the Sword Saint’s teachings and reached the Supreme Peak realm in his twenties, but even that could not erase the gulf created by age and experience.

hunks.baseline: First Fiend was an old monster from two generations back. He possessed immense internal energy, experience, and martial arts of the highest realm.
hunks.sol: First Fiend was an old monster from two generations past. He possessed immense internal energy, decades of experience, and martial arts of the highest order.

hunks.baseline: That was why, although he had been surprised at first, he had not felt any particular sense of danger.
hunks.sol: That was why, although he had been surprised at first, he had felt no real sense of danger.

hunks.baseline: *The Sword Saint raised quite a monster. There must have been a reason the Demon Lord warned me before he left. But he’s still far from being able to face this old man. Heh heh heh.*
hunks.sol: *The Sword Saint raised quite a monster. There was a reason the Demon Lord warned me about him before leaving. But he still has a long way to go before he can challenge this old man. Heh heh heh.*

hunks.baseline: However, it did not take long for the smile at the corners of his mouth to turn into fury.
hunks.sol: It did not take long, however, for the smile on his lips to twist into fury.

hunks.baseline: With a mad shout, the twin axes slashed down through the air. A net of Force spread wide and fell over Cheongpung’s head.
hunks.sol: With a maddened roar, he swept his twin axes down through the air. A vast net of Force unfurled and descended over Cheongpung’s head.

hunks.baseline: It was one of the signature techniques left behind by the Red Slaughter Demon, a fiend who had dyed the martial world red with blood three hundred years ago.
hunks.sol: It was one of the signature techniques left behind by the Red Slaughter Demon, who had dyed the martial world in blood three hundred years ago.

hunks.baseline: The unparalleled slaughter saint, pursued by the Central Plains Murim as a public enemy, had met his end in an unknown cave in the Qilian Mountains. The three brothers who had gone into hiding to escape the people of the martial world had learned the martial arts manual he left behind and emerged reborn as the Qilian Three Fiends.
hunks.sol: That infamous Slaughter Saint, hunted throughout the Central Plains as a public enemy of Murim, had met his end in an unnamed cave in the Qilian Mountains. Three brothers hiding there from the world had discovered the martial arts manual he left behind. After mastering its contents, they had emerged anew as the Qilian Three Fiends.

hunks.baseline: And now, the ultimate form of the Red Slaughter Asura Net—a technique no one had been able to perform since the Red Slaughter Demon—was finally being recreated through First Fiend’s twin axes.
hunks.sol: And now, the perfected Red Slaughter Asura Net—a technique no one since the Red Slaughter Demon had been able to perform—had finally reappeared through First Fiend’s twin axes.

hunks.baseline: That was when Cheongpung’s eyes sank deeply as he stared at the red Force net rushing toward him from every direction.
hunks.sol: That was when Cheongpung’s gaze deepened as he watched the red net of Force close in from every direction.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, purple Sword Force wrapped around the straight blade of his sword and sliced diagonally through the net of Force.
hunks.sol: At the same time, purple Sword Force enveloped his blade and sliced diagonally through the net.

hunks.baseline: Slice!
hunks.sol: Slash!

hunks.baseline: First Fiend’s mouth fell open as Cheongpung’s One-Character Wisdom Sword dismantled the ultimate Red Slaughter Asura Net with such ease.
hunks.sol: First Fiend’s mouth fell open as Cheongpung’s One-Character Wisdom Sword dismantled the perfected Red Slaughter Asura Net with absurd ease.

hunks.baseline: “You—you knew the Red Slaughter Demon’s martial arts?”
hunks.sol: “Y-You knew the Red Slaughter Demon’s martial arts?”

hunks.baseline: Every martial art left behind by the Red Slaughter Demon could be called a signature technique, but each clearly had weaknesses. Those weaknesses were a secret known only to the Qilian Three Fiends.
hunks.sol: Every martial art left by the Red Slaughter Demon deserved to be called a signature technique, but each still possessed weaknesses. Those weaknesses were secrets known only to the Qilian Three Fiends.

hunks.baseline: And yet the blood-brat before him had seen through them precisely.
hunks.sol: Yet the pup before him had identified them precisely.

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung’s reply came the next moment. It was short and simple.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung’s reply was short and simple.

hunks.baseline: “What’s the Red Slaughter Demon? I’ve never heard of him before.”
hunks.sol: “What’s the Red Slaughter Demon? I’ve never heard of him.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, is that why you’re upset?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, are you talking about what I just did?”

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung tilted his head and continued.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung tilted his head.

hunks.baseline: “It showed itself?”
hunks.sol: “Y-You could see it?”

hunks.baseline: “If you keep looking at something, you start to understand it. Grandpa has more internal energy than I do, and your martial arts are more complicated, so it took a little longer.”
hunks.sol: “If you keep watching, you start to understand. You have more internal energy than I do, Grandpa, and your martial arts are more complicated, so it took a little longer.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. But I don’t think I need to take that long anymore.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. But I don’t think it’ll take that long anymore.”

hunks.baseline: First Fiend understood what Cheongpung’s final words meant the next moment.
hunks.sol: First Fiend understood what Cheongpung meant the very next moment.

hunks.baseline: First Fiend hurriedly whirled the axes in both hands like lightning against the sword strike that came without warning.
hunks.sol: Caught off guard by the sudden sword strike, First Fiend hurriedly whipped both axes through the air like lightning.

hunks.baseline: The Red Slaughter Eighteen Axes lacked sophistication in its martial theory, but its destructive power was unparalleled. With more than two jiazi of internal energy added to it, its strength seemed capable of splitting heaven and earth.
hunks.sol: The Red Slaughter Eighteen Axes lacked subtlety, but its destructive power was second to none. Backed by more than two jiazi of internal energy, it carried enough force to split heaven and earth.

hunks.baseline: However…
hunks.sol: And yet—

hunks.baseline: The smoothly extending blade guided one axe blade aside. Then it struck the other axe that had been driving toward Cheongpung’s side.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung’s smoothly extended blade guided one axe aside, then struck the other as it swept powerfully toward his flank.

hunks.baseline: With a thunderous boom, First Fiend’s body staggered. He had effectively slammed the two axes in his own hands together. Even as he retreated, he could only stare in stunned disbelief.
hunks.sol: A thunderous boom erupted, and First Fiend staggered. He had effectively smashed his own axes together.
Even as he retreated, he stared in stunned disbelief.

hunks.baseline: *W-What on earth just happened?*
hunks.sol: *W-What in the world just happened?*

hunks.baseline: Pop!
hunks.sol: Fwoosh!

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung shot toward First Fiend.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung shot toward him.

hunks.baseline: His clear eyes had sunk deeply, and sunset-colored purple energy surged from the blade of his sword.
hunks.sol: His clear eyes had grown deep and still, while sunset-purple qi surged from his sword.

hunks.baseline: There was no mistake.
hunks.sol: There was no mistaking it.

hunks.baseline: The tremendous shock had slowed his reactions, but it was not enough to prevent him from countering.
hunks.sol: The revelation had slowed his reactions, but not enough to keep him from countering.

hunks.baseline: That was what he thought, at least—until Cheongpung’s sword moved.
hunks.sol: At least, that was what he believed—until Cheongpung’s sword moved.

hunks.baseline: A blunt, destructive sword technique descended gently like a falling flower. Thirty-six plum blossoms bloomed from the tip of the sword and fell through the air.
hunks.sol: The heavy, destructive sword stroke softened into the fall of a flower. Thirty-six plum blossoms bloomed from its tip and drifted down through the air.

hunks.baseline: A martial art surfaced in First Fiend’s mind.
hunks.sol: One martial art surfaced in First Fiend’s mind.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, he realized.
hunks.sol: At the same time, he realized—

hunks.baseline: Thirty-six plum blossoms—or rather, Force—wrapped around First Fiend’s entire body.
hunks.sol: Thirty-six plum blossoms—or rather, thirty-six streaks of Force—enveloped First Fiend’s entire body.

hunks.baseline: With blood spreading like mist, First Fiend staggered backward, his entire body covered in slashes.
hunks.sol: Blood spread like mist. Slashed from head to toe, First Fiend staggered backward.

hunks.baseline: Fear appeared in his eyes as he stared at Cheongpung, whose sword hung loosely at his side.
hunks.sol: Fear filled his eyes as he stared at Cheongpung, whose sword hung loosely at his side.

hunks.baseline: “It’s fortunate that it’s raining.”
hunks.sol: “Good thing it’s raining.”

hunks.baseline: Squelch.
hunks.sol: Splash.

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung’s foot stepped into a red puddle where raindrops and blood had mixed together. First Fiend let out a tearing scream.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung stepped into a crimson puddle of rainwater and blood. First Fiend let out a piercing scream.

hunks.baseline: “Anyone! Is there no one out there? Hurry, get this bastard…!”
hunks.sol: “Anyone! Is there no one out there? Hurry and kill this bastard…!”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t call out. There’s no one here.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t call for them. There’s no one left.”

hunks.baseline: There had been no footsteps and no sign of anyone’s presence.
hunks.sol: There had been no footsteps. No hint of anyone’s presence.

hunks.baseline: Slice!
hunks.sol: Slash!

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung flicked the blood from his sword, then stared with a rigid expression at *him*, standing tall before him.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung flicked the blood from his sword, then stared rigidly at the man standing before him.

hunks.baseline: “I want to ask you that instead. Who are you?”
hunks.sol: “I’d like to ask you the same thing. Who are you?”

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung continued in a faintly trembling voice.
hunks.sol: His voice trembled faintly as he continued.
